15: # Command Creation - Component Choice and Common Pitfalls
16: 
17: The first pitfall is building a command at all when a skill or agent fits better. Pick the component type, then check the draft against the recurring defects below.
18: 
19: ---
20: 
21: ## 1. OVERVIEW
22: 
23: This reference guards two failure modes: choosing the wrong component (a command when a skill or agent fits better) and the recurring command-authoring defects: missing gates, over-broad tools, dashboards in routers, and multiline descriptions. Decide the component first, then check the draft against the mistakes table.
24: 
25: ---
26: 
27: ## 2. PICK THE RIGHT COMPONENT FIRST
28: 
29: Choose the component type before drafting.
30: 
31: | Component | Primary Question | Use It When |
32: |---|---|---|
33: | Command | How should a user trigger this workflow? | A slash invocation should gather input and run a repeatable procedure |
34: | Skill | How should this work be done? | Reusable knowledge, standards, templates, or deep guidance are needed |
35: | Agent | Who should do this work? | A named persona needs authority, permissions, and operating rules |
36: 
37: **Practical rule**:
38: - create a command for a user-triggered workflow entry point
39: - create a skill for reusable knowledge or workflow doctrine
40: - create an agent for a durable runtime role with permissions
41: 
42: **Healthy pairing**:
43: - command gathers input and selects mode
44: - skill supplies detailed standards or patterns
45: - agent executes specialized work when delegation is appropriate
46: 
47: ---
48: 
49: ## 3. COMMON MISTAKES
50: 
51: | Mistake | Why It Breaks | Correct Fix |
52: |---|---|---|
53: | Creating a command for reference-only guidance | The slash command becomes a bloated manual instead of an executable workflow | Create or extend a skill/reference instead |
54: | Omitting `argument-hint` for required input | Users cannot see what the invocation expects | Add a precise hint with `<required>` and `[optional]` parts |
55: | Using a required hint without a gate | The command may infer missing input from context | Put the blocking gate after the H1 and its purpose line, before any workflow step |
56: | Treating `:auto` as permission to guess | Autonomous runs can fabricate missing decisions | Fail fast or ask targeted questions when required data is missing |
57: | Putting dashboards in the router | Routing logic becomes hard to audit and presentation cannot evolve independently | Move visible wording to `-presentation.txt` |
58: | Changing behavior while splitting presentation | A refactor becomes a hidden semantic change | Move wording without changing routing, modes, gates, or permissions |
59: | Over-broad `allowed-tools` | The command can use tools outside its contract | Reduce the list to the tools actually required |
60: | Using bare MCP names in `allowed-tools` | Runtime tool resolution can drift from the configured namespace | Use fully qualified `mcp__<server>__<tool>` IDs |
61: | Writing a multi-line description | Help output and metadata consumers expect a single-line summary | Keep `description` one line and move detail into the body |
62: | Adding workflow YAML to every split command | Direct-router command families may not need YAML execution assets | Add `-auto.yaml` and `-confirm.yaml` only when the family routes to workflow assets |
63: | Embedding rationale or meta-commentary in the router body | Design notes, prose-register/framework labels (e.g. "(COSTAR)"), benchmark timings, maintainer sync chores, or "no gap exists" self-attestations are noise a user sees rendered and drift from the truth | Keep the body behavioral. Move rationale to the decision-record/changelog and any render-style rule to the presentation asset |
64: 
65: ---
66: 
67: ## 4. RELATED RESOURCES
68: 
69: - [README.md](README.md) - command-creation reference map
70: - [argument-hints-and-modes.md](argument-hints-and-modes.md) - correct hint, mode, and frontmatter patterns
71: - [router-presentation-split.md](router-presentation-split.md) - the behavior-preserving split these mistakes violate
72: - [create-agent references](../../sk-create-agent/references/README.md) - sibling packet when the work is really an agent

2: title: Command Creation - Router / Presentation Split
3: description: How to separate a mode-based command into a thin router and its presentation asset — what each side owns, the before/after transformation, and the behavior-preserving rule.
4: trigger_phrases:
5:   - "router presentation split"
6:   - "thin router command"
7:   - "presentation asset command"
8:   - "split command refactor"
9:   - "behavior preserving command split"
10: importance_tier: normal
11: contextType: implementation
12: version: 1.0.0.5
13: ---
14: 
15: # Command Creation - Router / Presentation Split
16: 
17: Depth for SKILL.md Step 11. The split exists so routing behavior and visible wording can evolve independently: the router stays short and auditable, and the presentation asset becomes the display source of truth and can grow.
18: 
19: ---
20: 
21: ## 1. OVERVIEW
22: 
23: This reference expands the router/presentation separation named in SKILL.md Step 11: what the router owns, what the presentation asset owns, the mechanical before/after transformation, and the rule that a split must never change behavior.
24: 
25: ---
26: 
27: ## 2. WHAT EACH SIDE OWNS
28: 
29: **Router owns**:
30: - mandatory input gate or Phase 0
31: - owned-assets table
32: - mode detection and routing
33: - argument dispatch
34: - execution target selection
35: - presentation boundary statement
36: 
37: **Presentation owns**:
38: - startup questions and consolidated setup prompts
39: - dashboard and checkpoint layouts
40: - success and failure result templates
41: - next-step suggestions
42: - exact reply formats shown to the user
43: 
44: ---
45: 
46: ## 3. BEFORE / AFTER TRANSFORMATION
47: 
48: Move display wording out of the router and replace it with a pointer to the presentation asset.
49: 
50: Before:
51: 
52: ```markdown
53: ## 3. MODE ROUTING
54: 
55: If no mode suffix is present, ask:
56: "How should the review run? Choose A for auto or B for confirm."
57: 
58: After completion, show:
59: "Review complete. Next you can run /speckit:implement."
60: ```
61: 
62: After:
63: 
64: ```markdown
65: ## 3. MODE ROUTING
66: 
67: If no mode suffix is present, load `assets/review-packet-presentation.txt` and show the mode-selection prompt from `Startup Presentation`.
68: 
69: ## 5. PRESENTATION BOUNDARY
70: 
71: Result templates and next-step wording live only in `assets/review-packet-presentation.txt`.
72: ```
73: 
74: ---
75: 
76: ## 4. BEHAVIOR-PRESERVING RULE
77: 
78: Moving display text into the presentation asset must not change routing semantics, required inputs, confirmation behavior, or tool permissions. A presentation split is a relocation of wording, never a semantic change. If a refactor would alter routing, gates, modes, or `allowed-tools`, it is no longer a split — treat it as a behavior change and surface it explicitly.
79: 
80: ---
81: 
82: ## 5. RELATED RESOURCES
83: 
84: - [README.md](README.md) - command-creation reference map
85: - [worked-example.md](worked-example.md) - a complete router plus presentation asset following these rules
86: - [command-presentation-template.md](../assets/command-presentation-template.md) - full presentation asset skeleton

15: # Command Creation - Worked Split Example
16: 
17: A concrete end-to-end example of a mode-based namespace command. `sk-create-command/SKILL.md` owns the numbered workflow. This file shows what the finished output package looks like so you can model the shape.
18: 
19: ---
20: 
21: ## 1. OVERVIEW
22: 
23: This reference is a single worked example: the canonical command file contract and its invariants, then a full mode-based split showing both the router `.md` and its presentation `.txt`. It is illustrative overflow for SKILL.md Steps 5 and 11 (model the shape, do not treat `/review:packet` as a live command).
24: 
25: ---
26: 
27: ## 2. CANONICAL FILE CONTRACT
28: 
29: The smallest command package is one markdown file.
30: 
31: ```text
32: .skilled/commands/report.md             -> /report
33: .skilled/commands/review/packet.md      -> /review:packet
34: ```
35: 
36: Split mode-based workflow packages commonly use this shape:
37: 
38: ```text
39: .skilled/commands/review/packet.md
40: .skilled/commands/review/assets/review-packet-presentation.txt
41: .skilled/commands/review/assets/review-packet-auto.yaml
42: .skilled/commands/review/assets/review-packet-confirm.yaml
43: ```
44: 
45: **Invariants**:
46: - command and namespace names use lowercase hyphen-case
47: - the router `.md` owns routing, gates, mode resolution, and asset selection
48: - the presentation asset owns visible wording only
49: - workflow YAML exists only when the family routes execution through workflow assets
50: - direct-router families can omit workflow YAML and dispatch directly to tools or scripts
51: 
52: ---
53: 
54: ## 3. FULLY WORKED SPLIT EXAMPLE
55: 
56: This example is illustrative. It shows the output shape for a mode-based namespace command without claiming that `/review:packet` exists.
57: 
58: Router file: `.skilled/commands/review/packet.md`
59: 
60: ```markdown
61: ---
62: description: Review a spec packet with :auto or :confirm execution
63: argument-hint: "<spec-folder> [:auto|:confirm]"
64: allowed-tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash, Task
65: ---
66: 
67: # Review Packet Router
68: 
69: Thin router for `/review:packet`. The router resolves inputs and mode, loads owned assets, and selects the execution target. It does not own display templates.
70: 
71: ### MANDATORY FIRST ACTION - DO NOT SKIP
72: 
73: Before using any tools, inspect `$ARGUMENTS`.
74: 
75: If `$ARGUMENTS` is empty, undefined, whitespace-only, or contains only `:auto` / `:confirm`:
76: - stop immediately
77: - ask: "Which spec folder should be reviewed? Reply with a path such as `.opencode/specs/track/123-name`."
78: - wait for the user's answer
79: - use only `$ARGUMENTS` or that explicit answer as the spec folder
80: - do not infer the folder from conversation history, open files, or recent work
81: 
82: ---
83: 
84: ## 1. ROUTER CONTRACT
85: 
86: Inputs:
87: - `$ARGUMENTS` containing `<spec-folder>` and optional `:auto` or `:confirm`
88: 
89: Outputs:
90: - `STATUS=OK REVIEW=<summary>` when the review completes
91: - `STATUS=FAIL ERROR="<message>"` when required input, validation, or execution fails
92: - `STATUS=CANCELLED ACTION=cancelled` when the user cancels interactive execution
93: 
94: ## 2. OWNED ASSETS
95: 
96: | Purpose | Asset |
97: |---------|-------|
98: | Presentation source of truth | `assets/review-packet-presentation.txt` |
99: | Auto workflow | `assets/review-packet-auto.yaml` |
100: | Confirm workflow | `assets/review-packet-confirm.yaml` |
101: 
102: ## 3. MODE ROUTING
103: 
104: | Invocation | Mode | Behavior |
105: |---|---|---|
106: | `/review:packet:auto <spec-folder>` | AUTONOMOUS | Execute without approval gates; self-validate at checkpoints |
107: | `/review:packet:confirm <spec-folder>` | INTERACTIVE | Pause after each step for approval or adjustment |
108: | `/review:packet <spec-folder>` | PROMPT | Load presentation asset and ask the mode-selection prompt |
109: 
110: Parse the mode suffix first. After mode extraction, treat the remaining text as the spec folder.
111: 
112: ## 4. EXECUTION TARGETS
113: 
114: | Mode | Target |
115: |---|---|
116: | AUTONOMOUS | `assets/review-packet-auto.yaml` |
117: | INTERACTIVE | `assets/review-packet-confirm.yaml` |
118: | PROMPT | Use `assets/review-packet-presentation.txt` to ask for mode, then route to the selected target |
119: 
120: ## 5. PRESENTATION BOUNDARY
121: 
122: The router must not inline startup prompt wording, dashboard layouts, success templates, failure templates, or next-step suggestions. Load those from `assets/review-packet-presentation.txt`.
123: 
124: ## 6. WORKFLOW SUMMARY
125: 
126: Validate the spec folder, choose execution mode, run the selected review workflow, then return the structured status from the workflow result.
127: ```
128: 
129: Presentation asset: `.skilled/commands/review/assets/review-packet-presentation.txt`

132: # Review Packet Presentation Contract
133: 
134: Presentation source of truth for `/review:packet`. The router owns mode selection and asset loading. Workflow YAML owns execution. This file owns visible prompts, dashboard layout, and result displays.
135: 
136: ## 1. STARTUP PRESENTATION
137: 
138: For no suffix, ask once:
139: 
140: "How should the packet review run?"
141: 
142: | Option | Mode | Use When |
143: |---|---|---|
144: | A | Autonomous | The packet is low-risk and a full review can proceed without checkpoints |
145: | B | Interactive | You want to approve or adjust each review step |
146: 
147: Reply with `A` or `B`.
148: 
149: For `:auto`, do not show the mode prompt. Ask only if the spec folder is missing or invalid.
150: 
151: ### Auto Fail-Fast Display
152: 
153: `STATUS=FAIL ERROR="Missing required spec-folder for /review:packet:auto"`
154: 
155: ## 2. DASHBOARD / CHECKPOINT LAYOUT
156: 
157: | Step | Status | Evidence |
158: |---|---|---|
159: | Input verified | pending | spec folder path |
160: | Sources read | pending | files inspected |
161: | Findings checked | pending | review notes |
162: | Result emitted | pending | status line |
163: 
164: ## 3. RESULTS DISPLAY
165: 
166: ### Success
167: 
168: `STATUS=OK REVIEW="<summary>" FINDINGS=<count>`
169: 
170: ### Failure
171: 
172: `STATUS=FAIL ERROR="<message>"`
173: 
174: ## 4. NEXT-STEP SUGGESTIONS
175: 
176: | Condition | Suggested Command | Reason |
177: |---|---|---|
178: | Findings need implementation | `/speckit:implement <spec-folder>` | Continue from reviewed packet |
179: | Review needs more context | `/speckit:resume <spec-folder>` | Rehydrate packet context |
180: ```
181: 
182: ---
183: 
184: ## 4. RELATED RESOURCES

188: - [command-template.md](../assets/command-template.md) - command templates, gates, dispatch, modes, and validation checklist
189: - [command-presentation-template.md](../assets/command-presentation-template.md) - full presentation asset skeleton

630:     purpose: "Verify correctness and quality"
631:     depends_on: "phase_3_implementation"
632:     actions:
633:       - "Run full test suite"
634:       - "Check code quality metrics"
635:       - "Review against requirements"
636:     checkpoint: "quality_verified"
637:     validation_questions:
638:       - "Do all tests pass?"
639:       - "Are quality metrics met?"
640:       - "Does this satisfy the original request?"
641: ```
642: 
643: **Example in Markdown Reference**:
644: ```markdown
645: ### Implementation Workflow
646: 
647: You MUST complete each phase before proceeding to the next.
648: 
649: #### Phase 1: Preparation
650: 
651: **Purpose**: Gather context and analyze requirements
652: 
653: **Actions**:
654: 1. Read user request carefully
655: 2. Identify affected files and systems
656: 3. Review relevant documentation
657: 
658: **Validation**: `requirements_understood`
659: - Can I clearly explain what needs to be done?
660: - Do I know which files will change?
661: - Are there any unclear requirements?
662: 
663: #### Phase 2: Design
664: 
665: **Purpose**: Plan the implementation approach
666:

668: 1. Choose simplest solution that works
669: 2. Identify potential edge cases
670: 3. Plan validation strategy
671: 
672: **Validation**: `design_approved`
673: - Is this the simplest approach?
674: - Have I considered edge cases?
675: - Can I test this effectively?
676: 
677: [Continue with remaining phases...]
678: ```
679: 
680: ---
681: 
682: ## 5. CONVERTING LOGIC TO EXECUTABLE CODE
683: 
684: ### When to Extract Logic from Markdown
685: 
686: **Purpose**: Separate documentation from executable code for better maintainability, testability, and reusability.
687: 
688: **Decision Criteria**:
689: 
690: | Pattern Type          | Keep in Markdown  | Extract to Code           | Reasoning                                    |
691: | --------------------- | ----------------- | ------------------------- | -------------------------------------------- |
692: | **Python functions**  | ❌ No              | ✅ Yes → `/scripts/*.py`   | Type safety, unit testing, reusability       |
693: | **YAML configs**      | ❌ No              | ✅ Yes → `/assets/*.yaml`  | Dynamic loading, version control, validation |
694: | **Decision trees**    | ⚠️ High-level only | ✅ Details → YAML + Python | Machine-readable, can be validated           |
695: | **Command mappings**  | ⚠️ Examples only   | ✅ Full map → YAML         | Easier maintenance, can be imported          |
696: | **Workflow diagrams** | ✅ Yes (generated) | ✅ Source → YAML           | YAML = source of truth, diagram = output     |
697: | **Checklists**        | ✅ Yes             | ❌ No                      | Human-readable is primary use case           |
698: | **Before/after code** | ✅ Yes             | ❌ No                      | Educational, not executable                  |
699: 
700: ### Extraction Pattern
701: 
702: **In Markdown (Reference File)**:
703: ```markdown
704: ### [Workflow Name]
705: 
706: [High-level description of what the workflow does]
707: 
708: **Implementation:** See [workflow_name.py](../scripts/workflow_name.py) for execution logic and [workflow-config.yaml](../assets/workflow-config.yaml) for configuration.
709: 
710: **Quick Overview**:
711: 1. [Step 1 - high level]
712: 2. [Step 2 - high level]
713: 3. [Step 3 - high level]
714: 
715: **Configuration Options:**
716: - See YAML config for customizable parameters
717: - Default values optimized for common use cases
718: ```
719: 
720: ### Benefits of Separation
721: 
722: - **Type safety** - Python type hints catch errors at development time
723: - **Testability** - Unit tests for logic, integration tests for workflows
724: - **Reusability** - Imported by multiple skills or scripts
725: - **Version control** - Git diffs show logic changes clearly
726: - **Schema validation** - YAML can be validated against schemas
727: - **Dynamic loading** - Configuration changes without code edits
728: 
729: ### Example: Mode Detection Extraction
730: 
731: **❌ BEFORE** (inline Python in markdown):
732: \```python
733: def detect_mode(request):
734:     if '$quick' in request: return 'quick', 5
735:     elif '$ticket' in request: return 'ticket', 10
736:     return 'interactive', 10
737: \```
738: 
739: **✅ AFTER** (extracted with type safety):
740: 
741: `/scripts/mode_detection.py`:
742: \```python
743: from dataclasses import dataclass
744: 
745: @dataclass
746: class ModeConfig:
747:     mode: str
748:     depth_rounds: int
749: 
750: def detect_mode(request: str) -> ModeConfig:
751:     """Detect mode from command shortcuts."""
752:     if '$quick' in request:
753:         return ModeConfig('quick', 5)
754:     elif '$ticket' in request:
755:         return ModeConfig('ticket', 10)
756:     return ModeConfig('interactive', 10)
757: \```
758: 
759: `/tests/test_mode_detection.py`:
760: \```python
761: def test_quick_mode():
762:     assert detect_mode("$quick fix").mode == 'quick'
763: \```
764: 
765: **Why better:** Type hints, testable, reusable, separated from docs
766: 
767: ---
768: 
769: ## 6. YAML CONFIGURATION PATTERNS
770: 
771: ### Purpose
772: 
773: **YAML for configuration data** - Separate configuration from documentation for easier maintenance and dynamic loading.
774: 
775: **When to use YAML**:
776: - Configuration data (thresholds, mappings, rules)
777: - Data structures (nested objects, lists)
778: - Workflow definitions (step sequences, pipelines)
779: - Decision trees (conditional logic patterns)
780: - Validation schemas
781: 
782: ### Standard YAML Structure
783: 
784: ```yaml
785: # [config-name].yaml
786: metadata:
787:   version: "1.0.0"
788:   description: "Configuration for [feature name]"
789: 
790: config:
791:   threshold_values:
792:     low: 1
793:     medium: 5
794:     high: 10
795:   feature_flags:
796:     enable_feature_x: true
797:   mappings:
798:     $quick: "quick_mode"
799:     $ticket: "ticket_mode"
800: ```
801: 
802: ### File Organization
803: 
804: ```
805: .skilled/skills/[skill-name]/
806: ├── assets/
807: │   ├── workflow-configs/
808: │   │   ├── canvas-methodology.yaml
809: │   │   ├── variant-detection.yaml
810: │   │   └── complexity-scoring.yaml
811: │   ├── mappings/
812: │   │   ├── command-mappings.yaml
813: │   │   ├── mode-recognition.yaml
814: │   │   └── shortcut-definitions.yaml
815: │   └── templates/
816: │       └── [template files]
817: ```
818: 
819: ### Loading Pattern (Python)
820: 
821: ```python
822: import yaml
823: from pathlib import Path
824: 
825: def load_config(config_name: str) -> dict:
826:     """Load YAML config from assets directory."""
827:     config_path = Path(__file__).parent.parent / f"assets/{config_name}.yaml"
828:     with open(config_path) as f:
829:         return yaml.safe_load(f)['config']
830: 
831: # Usage
832: config = load_config("canvas-methodology")
833: ```
834: 
835: ### Example: Variant Detection Rules
836: 
837: **❌ BEFORE** (markdown table):
838: ```markdown
839: | Trigger                    | Action             |
840: | -------------------------- | ------------------ |
841: | "show options"             | Offer 3-5 variants |
842: | Complexity 7+ + "not sure" | Offer variants     |
843: ```
844: 
845: **✅ AFTER** (YAML + Python):
846: 
847: `/assets/variant-detection-rules.yaml`:
848: ```yaml
849: config:
850:   variant_triggers:
851:     explicit_keywords: ["show me options", "variations"]
852:     implicit:
853:       complexity_threshold: 7
854:       uncertainty_signals: ["not sure", "what would work"]
855:   variant_count:
856:     simple: [2, 3]
857:     complex: [5, 10]
858: ```
859: 
860: `/scripts/variant_detector.py`:
861: ```python
862: import yaml
863: 
864: class VariantDetector:
865:     def __init__(self, config_path: str):
866:         with open(config_path) as f:
867:             self.config = yaml.safe_load(f)['config']
868: 
869:     def should_generate_variants(self, request: str, complexity: int) -> bool:
870:         keywords = self.config['variant_triggers']['explicit_keywords']
871:         if any(kw in request.lower() for kw in keywords):
872:             return True
873: 
874:         threshold = self.config['variant_triggers']['implicit']['complexity_threshold']
875:         if complexity >= threshold:
876:             signals = self.config['variant_triggers']['implicit']['uncertainty_signals']
877:             return any(s in request.lower() for s in signals)
878:         return False
879: ```
880: 
881: **Why better:** Dynamic config loading, easier maintenance, schema validation possible
882: 
883: ---
884: 
885: ## 7. PYTHON SCRIPT INTEGRATION
886: 
887: ### When to Use Python for Logic
888: 
889: **Use Python scripts when**:
890: - Procedural logic (workflows, algorithms)
891: - Complex conditionals (multi-step decisions)
892: - Data transformation (processing, validation)
893: - API integration (external services)
894: - File operations (reading, parsing, generating)
895: 
896: ### Type Hints and Docstring Standards
897: 
898: **Always include**:
899: - Type hints for parameters and return values
900: - Google-style docstrings (Args, Returns, Raises, Examples)
901: - Dataclasses for structured data
902: 
903: **Example**:
904: ```python
905: from dataclasses import dataclass
906: from pathlib import Path
907: 
908: @dataclass
909: class ValidationResult:
910:     is_valid: bool
911:     errors: list[str]
912: 
913: def validate_config(config_path: Path) -> ValidationResult:
914:     """
915:     Validate configuration file.
916: 
917:     Args:
918:         config_path: Path to YAML config file
919: 
920:     Returns:
921:         ValidationResult with status and errors
922: 
923:     Raises:
924:         FileNotFoundError: If config doesn't exist
925:     """
926:     if not config_path.exists():
927:         raise FileNotFoundError(f"Config not found: {config_path}")
928:     # Validation logic
929:     return ValidationResult(is_valid=True, errors=[])
930: ```
931: 
932: ### Unit Testing Requirements
933: 
934: **Every Python script must have tests**:
935: - Naming: `test_[script_name].py` in `/tests/` directory
936: - Coverage: ≥80% line coverage
937: - Framework: pytest
938: 
939: **Example**:
940: ```python
941: import pytest
942: from scripts.config_validator import validate_config
943: 
944: def test_validate_success(tmp_path):
945:     config = tmp_path / "config.yaml"
946:     config.write_text("config:\n  threshold: 5")
947:     result = validate_config(config)
948:     assert result.is_valid
949: 
950: def test_validate_missing_file():
951:     with pytest.raises(FileNotFoundError):
952:         validate_config(Path("nonexistent.yaml"))
953: ```
954: 
955: ### Import and Reference Patterns
956: 
957: **Python import order**: Standard library → Third-party → Local
958: 
959: **Markdown references**:
960: ```markdown
961: **See also:** [script_name.py](../scripts/script_name.py), [config.yaml](../assets/config.yaml)
962: ```
963: 
964: ### Example: Workflow Decision Logic
965: 
966: **❌ BEFORE** (text decision tree):
967: ```markdown
968: IF "$quick": use quick mode (5 rounds)
969: IF "$ticket": use ticket mode (10 rounds)
970: OTHERWISE: use interactive mode
971: ```
972: 
973: **✅ AFTER** (Python with type safety):
974: 
975: `/scripts/workflow_router.py`:
976: ```python
977: from typing import Literal
978: from dataclasses import dataclass
979: 
980: WorkflowMode = Literal["quick", "ticket", "interactive"]
981: 
982: @dataclass
983: class WorkflowDecision:
984:     mode: WorkflowMode
985:     depth_rounds: int
986: 
987: def route_workflow(request: str) -> WorkflowDecision:
988:     """Route request to appropriate workflow."""
989:     if '$quick' in request.lower():
990:         return WorkflowDecision("quick", 5)
991:     if '$ticket' in request.lower():
992:         return WorkflowDecision("ticket", 10)
993:     return WorkflowDecision("interactive", 10)
994: ```
995: 
996: `/tests/test_workflow_router.py`:
997: ```python
998: def test_quick_mode():
999:     assert route_workflow("$quick fix").mode == "quick"
1000: 
1001: def test_default_mode():
1002:     assert route_workflow("help me").mode == "interactive"
1003: ```
1004: 
1005: **Why better:** Type-safe with Literal, testable, structured with dataclass
1006: 
1007: ---
1008: 
1009: ## 8. STANDARD STRUCTURE TEMPLATE
1010: 
1011: ### Complete Skill Directory Structure
1012: 
1013: **Path:** `.skilled/skills/` (singular, not `skills` or `openskills`)
1014: 
1015: ```
1016: .skilled/skills/[skill-name]/
1017: ├── SKILL.md                    # Main skill file (Level 2 in progressive disclosure)
1018: ├── references/                 # Deep-dive technical documentation (Level 3)
1019: │   ├── workflow-name.md        # Multi-phase workflows with checkpoints (kebab-case)
1020: │   ├── patterns-library.md     # Before/after code patterns (kebab-case)
1021: │   ├── debugging-guide.md      # Systematic troubleshooting (kebab-case)
1022: │   └── quick-reference.md      # Commands, shortcuts, checklists (kebab-case)
1023: ├── scripts/                    # Executable Python logic
1024: │   ├── mode_detection.py       # Procedural logic, algorithms
1025: │   ├── workflow_router.py      # Decision logic
1026: │   ├── config_validator.py     # Data transformation
1027: │   └── __init__.py             # Package initialization
1028: ├── assets/                     # Configuration and data files
1029: │   ├── workflow-configs/       # YAML workflow definitions
1030: │   │   ├── canvas-methodology.yaml
1031: │   │   └── complexity-scoring.yaml
1032: │   ├── mappings/               # YAML mapping data
1033: │   │   ├── command-mappings.yaml
1034: │   │   └── mode-recognition.yaml
1035: │   └── templates/              # Markdown/code templates
1036: │       ├── template-name.md
1037: │       └── component-template.tsx
1038: └── tests/                      # Unit and integration tests
1039:     ├── test_mode_detection.py
1040:     ├── test_workflow_router.py
1041:     ├── test_config_validator.py
1042:     └── __init__.py
1043: ```
1044: 
1045: ### Directory Purposes
1046: 
1047: **SKILL.md** (Required): Overview, workflow (3-5 steps), rules. Target: <200 lines
1048: 
1049: **references/** (Optional): Detailed workflows, patterns, debugging. Target: 500-3000 lines/file. **All authored filenames must use kebab-case.**
1050: 
1051: **scripts/** (Optional): Python logic - procedural, routing, validation. Requires type hints, tests
1052: 
1053: **assets/** (Optional): YAML configs, workflow definitions, templates, mappings
1054: 
1055: **tests/** (Required if scripts/ exists): Unit tests with ≥80% coverage, pytest, `test_[name].py`
1056: 
1057: ### When to Create Each Directory
1058: 
1059: | Directory     | Create When                                                     | Don't Create When                           |
1060: | ------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------- |
1061: | `references/` | Content >200 lines, multi-phase workflows, systematic debugging | Simple skills <200 lines total              |
1062: | `scripts/`    | Python logic extracted from markdown, reusable functions        | Pure documentation, no executable logic     |
1063: | `assets/`     | YAML configs, templates, structured data                        | No configuration data, inline examples only |
1064: | `tests/`      | `scripts/` directory exists                                     | No Python scripts to test                   |
1065: 
1066: ### Integration Pattern
1067: 
1068: **How components work together:**
1069: - SKILL.md references scripts: `[workflow_router.py](./scripts/workflow_router.py)`
1070: - Scripts load configs: `yaml.safe_load(f"../assets/config.yaml")`
1071: - Tests verify scripts: `assert route_workflow("input").mode == "expected"`
1072: - Markdown links to all: "See [script.py](../scripts/), [config.yaml](../assets/)"

38: ## 2. DOCUMENT STRUCTURE
39: 
40: ### Document Structure: Title and Intro
41: 
42: **CRITICAL: The intro after the H1 title must be 1-2 SHORT sentences only.**
43: 
44: ```markdown
45: ---
46: title: [Title]
47: description: [One-line description - same as intro]
48: trigger_phrases:
49:   - "[distinctive phrase one]"
50:   - "[distinctive phrase two]"
51:   - "[distinctive phrase three]"
52: importance_tier: normal
53: contextType: general
54: version: 1.0.0.0
55: ---
56: 
57: # [Title]
58: 
59: [1-2 SHORT sentences only. Brief hook/summary. NO subsections, NO headers here.]
60: 
61: ---
62: 
63: \## 1. OVERVIEW
64: [All detailed content goes here, NOT in the intro]
65: 
66: ```
67: 
68: Every reference file carries this full 5-field frontmatter block: the Skill Advisor harvests it as routing signal (3-8 lowercase multi-word `trigger_phrases` drawn from the doc's content. `importance_tier` defaults to `normal`, with `important` only for formal contract docs. `contextType` is one of `planning|research|implementation|general`). See [frontmatter-templates.md](../../../sk-create-frontmatter/assets/frontmatter-templates.md) for field rules.

76: # Git Commit Workflows
77: 
78: This reference turns a mixed working tree into a small set of reviewable commits.
79:

81:

83: 
84: ### Purpose
85: Each rule keeps one commit focused on one intent, so history stays easy to read, review and revert.
86: 
87: ### When to Use
88: - Creating commits with multiple file changes
89: - Filtering generated files from commits
90: - Writing clear commit messages

94: ```

193: - Core Principle, Boundaries and Key Sources follow Purpose and When to Use, in that order, and each appears only when it has content.

202: ### What Are AI Agent Skill Reference Files?
203: 
204: Reference files are detailed technical documentation in the `references/` directory that provide deep-dive guidance with **explicit reasoning** - making thought processes visible, showing decision logic, and analyzing root causes.
205: 
206: **Core Purpose**:
207: - **Technical depth** - Step-by-step reasoning with rationale
208: - **Phased workflows** - Structured processes with validation checkpoints
209: - **Pattern libraries** - Before/after examples, comparison tables
210: - **Tool integration** - MCP tools, scripts, asset references
211: - **Root cause analysis** - Systematic debugging and troubleshooting
212: 
213: **Key Difference from Generic Documentation**:
214: - AI agent skills = Actionable workflows with explicit reasoning
215: - Generic docs = Information reference without decision logic
216: 
217: ### Progressive Disclosure in Skills
218: 
219: ```
220: Level 1: Metadata (name + description)
221:          └─ Always in context (~100 words)
222:             ↓
223: Level 2: SKILL.md body
224:          └─ When skill triggers (<5k words)
225:             ↓
226: Level 3: Reference files (this document)
227:          └─ Loaded as needed (500-3000 lines per file)
228: ```
229: 
230: **Reference files = Level 3**: Deep technical guidance loaded only when the agent needs specific workflow details.

682: ## 5. CONVERTING LOGIC TO EXECUTABLE CODE
683: 
684: ### When to Extract Logic from Markdown
685: 
686: **Purpose**: Separate documentation from executable code for better maintainability, testability, and reusability.
687: 
688: **Decision Criteria**:
689: 
690: | Pattern Type          | Keep in Markdown  | Extract to Code           | Reasoning                                    |
691: | --------------------- | ----------------- | ------------------------- | -------------------------------------------- |
692: | **Python functions**  | ❌ No              | ✅ Yes → `/scripts/*.py`   | Type safety, unit testing, reusability       |
693: | **YAML configs**      | ❌ No              | ✅ Yes → `/assets/*.yaml`  | Dynamic loading, version control, validation |
694: | **Decision trees**    | ⚠️ High-level only | ✅ Details → YAML + Python | Machine-readable, can be validated           |
695: | **Command mappings**  | ⚠️ Examples only   | ✅ Full map → YAML         | Easier maintenance, can be imported          |
696: | **Workflow diagrams** | ✅ Yes (generated) | ✅ Source → YAML           | YAML = source of truth, diagram = output     |
697: | **Checklists**        | ✅ Yes             | ❌ No                      | Human-readable is primary use case           |
698: | **Before/after code** | ✅ Yes             | ❌ No                      | Educational, not executable                  |
699: 
700: ### Extraction Pattern
701: 
702: **In Markdown (Reference File)**:
703: ```markdown
704: ### [Workflow Name]
705: 
706: [High-level description of what the workflow does]
707: 
708: **Implementation:** See [workflow_name.py](../scripts/workflow_name.py) for execution logic and [workflow-config.yaml](../assets/workflow-config.yaml) for configuration.
709: 
710: **Quick Overview**:
711: 1. [Step 1 - high level]
712: 2. [Step 2 - high level]
713: 3. [Step 3 - high level]
714: 
715: **Configuration Options:**
716: - See YAML config for customizable parameters
717: - Default values optimized for common use cases
718: ```
719: 
720: ### Benefits of Separation
721: 
722: - **Type safety** - Python type hints catch errors at development time
723: - **Testability** - Unit tests for logic, integration tests for workflows
724: - **Reusability** - Imported by multiple skills or scripts
725: - **Version control** - Git diffs show logic changes clearly
726: - **Schema validation** - YAML can be validated against schemas
727: - **Dynamic loading** - Configuration changes without code edits
728: 
729: ### Example: Mode Detection Extraction
730: 
731: **❌ BEFORE** (inline Python in markdown):
732: \```python
733: def detect_mode(request):
734:     if '$quick' in request: return 'quick', 5
735:     elif '$ticket' in request: return 'ticket', 10
736:     return 'interactive', 10
737: \```
738: 
739: **✅ AFTER** (extracted with type safety):
740: 
741: `/scripts/mode_detection.py`:
742: \```python
743: from dataclasses import dataclass
744: 
745: @dataclass
746: class ModeConfig:
747:     mode: str
748:     depth_rounds: int
749: 
750: def detect_mode(request: str) -> ModeConfig:
751:     """Detect mode from command shortcuts."""
752:     if '$quick' in request:
753:         return ModeConfig('quick', 5)
754:     elif '$ticket' in request:
755:         return ModeConfig('ticket', 10)
756:     return ModeConfig('interactive', 10)
757: \```
758: 
759: `/tests/test_mode_detection.py`:
760: \```python
761: def test_quick_mode():
762:     assert detect_mode("$quick fix").mode == 'quick'
763: \```
764: 
765: **Why better:** Type hints, testable, reusable, separated from docs
766:

769: ## 6. YAML CONFIGURATION PATTERNS
770: 
771: ### Purpose
772: 
773: **YAML for configuration data** - Separate configuration from documentation for easier maintenance and dynamic loading.
774: 
775: **When to use YAML**:
776: - Configuration data (thresholds, mappings, rules)
777: - Data structures (nested objects, lists)
778: - Workflow definitions (step sequences, pipelines)
779: - Decision trees (conditional logic patterns)
780: - Validation schemas
781: 
782: ### Standard YAML Structure
783: 
784: ```yaml
785: # [config-name].yaml
786: metadata:
787:   version: "1.0.0"
788:   description: "Configuration for [feature name]"
789: 
790: config:
791:   threshold_values:
792:     low: 1
793:     medium: 5
794:     high: 10
795:   feature_flags:
796:     enable_feature_x: true
797:   mappings:
798:     $quick: "quick_mode"
799:     $ticket: "ticket_mode"
800: ```
801: 
802: ### File Organization
803: 
804: ```
805: .skilled/skills/[skill-name]/
806: ├── assets/
807: │   ├── workflow-configs/
808: │   │   ├── canvas-methodology.yaml
809: │   │   ├── variant-detection.yaml
810: │   │   └── complexity-scoring.yaml
811: │   ├── mappings/
812: │   │   ├── command-mappings.yaml
813: │   │   ├── mode-recognition.yaml
814: │   │   └── shortcut-definitions.yaml
815: │   └── templates/
816: │       └── [template files]
817: ```
818: 
819: ### Loading Pattern (Python)
820: 
821: ```python
822: import yaml
823: from pathlib import Path
824: 
825: def load_config(config_name: str) -> dict:
826:     """Load YAML config from assets directory."""
827:     config_path = Path(__file__).parent.parent / f"assets/{config_name}.yaml"
828:     with open(config_path) as f:
829:         return yaml.safe_load(f)['config']
830: 
831: # Usage
832: config = load_config("canvas-methodology")
833: ```
834: 
835: ### Example: Variant Detection Rules
836: 
837: **❌ BEFORE** (markdown table):
838: ```markdown
839: | Trigger                    | Action             |
840: | -------------------------- | ------------------ |
841: | "show options"             | Offer 3-5 variants |
842: | Complexity 7+ + "not sure" | Offer variants     |
843: ```
844: 
845: **✅ AFTER** (YAML + Python):
846: 
847: `/assets/variant-detection-rules.yaml`:
848: ```yaml
849: config:
850:   variant_triggers:
851:     explicit_keywords: ["show me options", "variations"]
852:     implicit:
853:       complexity_threshold: 7
854:       uncertainty_signals: ["not sure", "what would work"]
855:   variant_count:
856:     simple: [2, 3]
857:     complex: [5, 10]
858: ```
859: 
860: `/scripts/variant_detector.py`:
861: ```python
862: import yaml
863: 
864: class VariantDetector:
865:     def __init__(self, config_path: str):
866:         with open(config_path) as f:
867:             self.config = yaml.safe_load(f)['config']
868: 
869:     def should_generate_variants(self, request: str, complexity: int) -> bool:
870:         keywords = self.config['variant_triggers']['explicit_keywords']
871:         if any(kw in request.lower() for kw in keywords):
872:             return True
873: 
874:         threshold = self.config['variant_triggers']['implicit']['complexity_threshold']
875:         if complexity >= threshold:
876:             signals = self.config['variant_triggers']['implicit']['uncertainty_signals']
877:             return any(s in request.lower() for s in signals)
878:         return False
879: ```
880: 
881: **Why better:** Dynamic config loading, easier maintenance, schema validation possible
882:

885: ## 7. PYTHON SCRIPT INTEGRATION
886: 
887: ### When to Use Python for Logic
888: 
889: **Use Python scripts when**:
890: - Procedural logic (workflows, algorithms)
891: - Complex conditionals (multi-step decisions)
892: - Data transformation (processing, validation)
893: - API integration (external services)
894: - File operations (reading, parsing, generating)
895: 
896: ### Type Hints and Docstring Standards
897: 
898: **Always include**:
899: - Type hints for parameters and return values
900: - Google-style docstrings (Args, Returns, Raises, Examples)
901: - Dataclasses for structured data
902: 
903: **Example**:
904: ```python
905: from dataclasses import dataclass
906: from pathlib import Path
907: 
908: @dataclass
909: class ValidationResult:
910:     is_valid: bool
911:     errors: list[str]
912: 
913: def validate_config(config_path: Path) -> ValidationResult:
914:     """
915:     Validate configuration file.
916: 
917:     Args:
918:         config_path: Path to YAML config file
919: 
920:     Returns:
921:         ValidationResult with status and errors
922: 
923:     Raises:
924:         FileNotFoundError: If config doesn't exist
925:     """
926:     if not config_path.exists():
927:         raise FileNotFoundError(f"Config not found: {config_path}")
928:     # Validation logic
929:     return ValidationResult(is_valid=True, errors=[])
930: ```
931: 
932: ### Unit Testing Requirements
933: 
934: **Every Python script must have tests**:
935: - Naming: `test_[script_name].py` in `/tests/` directory
936: - Coverage: ≥80% line coverage
937: - Framework: pytest
938: 
939: **Example**:
940: ```python
941: import pytest
942: from scripts.config_validator import validate_config
943: 
944: def test_validate_success(tmp_path):
945:     config = tmp_path / "config.yaml"
946:     config.write_text("config:\n  threshold: 5")
947:     result = validate_config(config)
948:     assert result.is_valid
949: 
950: def test_validate_missing_file():
951:     with pytest.raises(FileNotFoundError):
952:         validate_config(Path("nonexistent.yaml"))
953: ```
954: 
955: ### Import and Reference Patterns
956: 
957: **Python import order**: Standard library → Third-party → Local
958: 
959: **Markdown references**:
960: ```markdown
961: **See also:** [script_name.py](../scripts/script_name.py), [config.yaml](../assets/config.yaml)
962: ```
963: 
964: ### Example: Workflow Decision Logic
965: 
966: **❌ BEFORE** (text decision tree):
967: ```markdown
968: IF "$quick": use quick mode (5 rounds)
969: IF "$ticket": use ticket mode (10 rounds)
970: OTHERWISE: use interactive mode
971: ```
972: 
973: **✅ AFTER** (Python with type safety):
974: 
975: `/scripts/workflow_router.py`:
976: ```python
977: from typing import Literal
978: from dataclasses import dataclass
979: 
980: WorkflowMode = Literal["quick", "ticket", "interactive"]
981: 
982: @dataclass
983: class WorkflowDecision:
984:     mode: WorkflowMode
985:     depth_rounds: int
986: 
987: def route_workflow(request: str) -> WorkflowDecision:
988:     """Route request to appropriate workflow."""
989:     if '$quick' in request.lower():

991:     if '$ticket' in request.lower():
992:         return WorkflowDecision("ticket", 10)
993:     return WorkflowDecision("interactive", 10)

1001: def test_default_mode():
1002:     assert route_workflow("help me").mode == "interactive"
1003: ```

1009: ## 8. STANDARD STRUCTURE TEMPLATE
1010: 
1011: ### Complete Skill Directory Structure
1012: 
1013: **Path:** `.skilled/skills/` (singular, not `skills` or `openskills`)
1014: 
1015: ```
1016: .skilled/skills/[skill-name]/
1017: ├── SKILL.md                    # Main skill file (Level 2 in progressive disclosure)
1018: ├── references/                 # Deep-dive technical documentation (Level 3)
1019: │   ├── workflow-name.md        # Multi-phase workflows with checkpoints (kebab-case)
1020: │   ├── patterns-library.md     # Before/after code patterns (kebab-case)
1021: │   ├── debugging-guide.md      # Systematic troubleshooting (kebab-case)
1022: │   └── quick-reference.md      # Commands, shortcuts, checklists (kebab-case)
1023: ├── scripts/                    # Executable Python logic
1024: │   ├── mode_detection.py       # Procedural logic, algorithms
1025: │   ├── workflow_router.py      # Decision logic
1026: │   ├── config_validator.py     # Data transformation
1027: │   └── __init__.py             # Package initialization
1028: ├── assets/                     # Configuration and data files
1029: │   ├── workflow-configs/       # YAML workflow definitions
1030: │   │   ├── canvas-methodology.yaml
1031: │   │   └── complexity-scoring.yaml
1032: │   ├── mappings/               # YAML mapping data
1033: │   │   ├── command-mappings.yaml
1034: │   │   └── mode-recognition.yaml
1035: │   └── templates/              # Markdown/code templates
1036: │       ├── template-name.md
1037: │       └── component-template.tsx
1038: └── tests/                      # Unit and integration tests
1039:     ├── test_mode_detection.py

1045: ### Directory Purposes
1046: 
1047: **SKILL.md** (Required): Overview, workflow (3-5 steps), rules. Target: <200 lines
1048: 
1049: **references/** (Optional): Detailed workflows, patterns, debugging. Target: 500-3000 lines/file. **All authored filenames must use kebab-case.**
1050: 
1051: **scripts/** (Optional): Python logic - procedural, routing, validation. Requires type hints, tests
1052: 
1053: **assets/** (Optional): YAML configs, workflow definitions, templates, mappings

1055: **tests/** (Required if scripts/ exists): Unit tests with ≥80% coverage, pytest, `test_[name].py`

1063: | `assets/`     | YAML configs, templates, structured data                        | No configuration data, inline examples only |
1064: | `tests/`      | `scripts/` directory exists                                     | No Python scripts to test                   |

15: # Command Creation - Argument Hints and Modes
16: 
17: Depth for SKILL.md Steps 6 and 10: the surface where a command declares its inputs. Use these patterns when writing `argument-hint`, choosing `:auto`/`:confirm` behavior, or tightening frontmatter.
18: 
19: ---
20: 
21: ## 1. OVERVIEW
22: 
23: This reference collects the input-declaration patterns that would bloat the SKILL.md workflow: a catalog of `argument-hint` shapes, the design intent behind `:auto`/`:confirm` modes, and budget-minded frontmatter tips for `description` and `allowed-tools`.
24: 
25: ---
26: 
27: ## 2. ARGUMENT-HINT DESIGN PATTERNS
28: 
29: Use `argument-hint` when the command expects user input. Required arguments use angle brackets. Optional arguments use square brackets. Mode suffixes such as `[:auto|:confirm]` are optional selectors, not required content.
30: 
31: | Pattern | Example | Use When |
32: |---|---|---|
33: | Required subject | `"<spec-folder>"` | The command cannot run without one primary input |
34: | Required plus optional mode | `"<request> [:auto|:confirm]"` | Mode selection changes execution pace |
35: | Optional action or query | `"[action|query] [options]"` | Empty input can show help or use a safe default |
36: | Required target plus flags | `"<path> [--dry-run] [--confirm]"` | Flags alter safety or preview behavior |
37: | Namespace operation | `"<skill-name> [--validate]"` | The namespace/action is in the invocation path, not the hint |
38: 
39: **Good hints**:
40: - `"<task> [:auto|:confirm]"`
41: - `"<spec-folder> [--strict]"`
42: - `"[status|repair|validate] [target]"`
43: 
44: **Weak hints**:
45: - `"args"` because it does not tell the user what to provide
46: - `"<optional-target>"` because required syntax contradicts the word optional
47: - `"<query> [query]"` because it duplicates the same concept in two forms
48: 
49: Mandatory-gate reminder: when the hint contains any required `<argument>`, the command needs a blocking input gate after the H1 and its purpose line, before any workflow step. The gate must ignore mode suffixes when deciding whether real required content exists.
50: 
51: ---
52: 
53: ## 3. `:auto` VS `:confirm` MODE DESIGN
54: 
55: Use modes when the same workflow needs different execution pacing.
56: 
57: | Mode | Design Intent | Good Fit |
58: |---|---|---|
59: | `:auto` | Execute without approval gates, self-validating at checkpoints | Low-risk repeatable workflows with clear defaults |
60: | `:confirm` | Pause after steps for user approval, modification, skip, or abort | Workflows with ambiguity, review checkpoints, or higher risk |
61: | no suffix | Ask the user to choose mode | Commands where neither pace is universally safe |
62: 
63: `:auto` should still stop when required input is missing, destructive impact is unclear, or a default would be fabricated. Autonomous does not mean permission to invent.
64: 
65: `:confirm` should not ask tiny repetitive questions. Batch setup into one consolidated prompt, then pause at meaningful checkpoints.
66: 
67: If a command combines modes with argument dispatch, parse mode first and dispatch the remaining arguments after removing the suffix.
68: 
69: ---
70: 
71: ## 4. FRONTMATTER AND DESCRIPTION BUDGET TIPS
72: 
73: Every command needs YAML frontmatter with a single-line `description`. Add `argument-hint` and `allowed-tools` when applicable.
74: 
75: ```yaml
76: ---
77: description: Review a spec packet with :auto or :confirm execution
78: argument-hint: "<spec-folder> [:auto|:confirm]"
79: allowed-tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash, Task
80: ---
81: ```
82: 
83: **Description tips**:
84: - start with an action verb when possible
85: - keep it concise and single-line
86: - target 110 characters or less
87: - retain important trigger tokens such as `:auto` and `:confirm` when they are part of the command contract
88: - do not use YAML block scalars for `description`
89: - avoid product lists or implementation detail that belongs in the body
90: 
91: **Allowed-tools tips**:
92: - list only tools the command actually uses
93: - do not add broad tools just in case
94: - use fully qualified MCP IDs in `allowed-tools`, such as `mcp__<server>__<tool>`
95: - use bare MCP tool names only in prose, not in frontmatter
96: 
97: ---
98: 
99: ## 5. RELATED RESOURCES
100: 
101: - [README.md](README.md) - command-creation reference map
102: - [worked-example.md](worked-example.md) - frontmatter and gate applied in a full command
103: - [common-pitfalls.md](common-pitfalls.md) - hint, mode, and frontmatter mistakes with fixes

**Purpose**: [Description of what this command accomplishes.]

### 🚨 MANDATORY FIRST ACTION - DO NOT SKIP

[Include the Mandatory Gate Pattern]

## 1. USER INPUT

\`\`\`text
$ARGUMENTS

---

## 2. MODE DETECTION & ROUTING

### Step 1: Parse Mode Suffix

Detect execution mode from command invocation:

| Pattern                | Mode        | Behavior                                      |
| ---------------------- | ----------- | --------------------------------------------- |
| `/command:auto`        | AUTONOMOUS  | Execute all steps without user approval gates |
| `/command:confirm`     | INTERACTIVE | Pause at each step for user approval          |
| `/command` (no suffix) | PROMPT      | Ask user to choose mode                       |

### Step 2: Mode Selection (when no suffix detected)

If no `:auto` or `:confirm` suffix is present, present options to user:

**Question**: "How would you like to execute this workflow?"

| Option | Mode        | Description                                                    |
| ------ | ----------- | -------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **A**  | Autonomous  | Execute all steps without approval gates. Best for [use case]. |
| **B**  | Interactive | Pause at each step for approval. Best for [use case].          |

**Wait for user response before proceeding.**

### Step 3: Transform Raw Input

Parse the raw text from `$ARGUMENTS` and transform into structured fields.

---

## 3. KEY BEHAVIORS

### Autonomous Mode (`:auto`)
- Executes all steps without user approval gates
- Self-validates at each checkpoint
- Makes informed decisions based on best judgment
- Documents all significant decisions

### Interactive Mode (`:confirm`)
- Pauses after each step for user approval
- Presents options: Approve, Review Details, Modify, Skip, Abort
- Documents user decisions at each checkpoint
- Allows course correction throughout workflow

---

## 4. CONTEXT LOADING

When resuming work in an existing spec folder, prompt to load prior session memory:
- **A)** Load most recent memory file (quick context refresh)
- **B)** Load all recent files (up to 3) (comprehensive context)
- **C)** List all files and select specific (historical search)
- **D)** Skip (start fresh, no context)

---

## 5. EXAMPLES

**Example 1: Autonomous execution**
\`\`\`
/command:auto [arguments]
\`\`\`

**Example 2: Interactive execution**
\`\`\`
/command:confirm [arguments]
\`\`\`

**Example 3: Prompt for mode selection**
\`\`\`
/command [arguments]
\`\`\`
```

308: ### Step 11: Author The Router As A First-Class Command Type
309: 
310: A router is a first-class command type, not a loose refactor. Its `.md` is a thin dispatcher: verify the orchestrating agent, resolve mode and arguments, then hand off to owned assets (a presentation `.txt`, optional `-auto.yaml` / `-confirm.yaml`, or scripts). It carries no inline dashboards, prompts, or result templates.
311: 
312: **Detection signature.** The validator treats a command as a router when any of:
313: 
314: - a `render-command-contract` marker is present (the compiled-stub variant, which has no authored section requirements), or
315: - a `Presentation Boundary` section is present, or
316: - two or more of `{Router Contract, Owned Assets, Mode Routing, Execution Targets}` co-occur.
317: 
318: **Minimal core vs recommended.** A router must include the blocking core only: `Owned Assets` and `Presentation Boundary`.
319: The remaining canonical sections (`Router Contract`, `Mode Routing`, `Execution Targets`, `Workflow Summary`) are recommended and surface as non-blocking warnings when absent.
320: Author the full shape for new routers.
321: The minimal core lets incremental migrations land without failing.
322: 
323: **Canonical vocabulary (numbered `## N.`, full integers).** Use exactly these H2 names, in this order, for a fully-shaped router:
324: 
325: ```text
326: ## 1. ROUTER CONTRACT
327: ## 2. OWNED ASSETS
328: ## 3. MODE ROUTING
329: ## 4. EXECUTION TARGETS
330: ## 5. PRESENTATION BOUNDARY
331: ## 6. WORKFLOW SUMMARY
332: ```
333: 
334: Do not invent divergent synonyms (`Routing Assets`, `Workflow Routing`, `Execution Order`). The validator alias-normalizes those as a safety net, but the authored end state is the canonical names above.
335: 
336: **Ownership boundary.** The router owns:
337: - the mandatory input gate or Phase 0.
338: - the owned-assets table, mode resolution and argument routing.
339: - execution-target selection and the presentation boundary.
340: - a short workflow summary.
341: 
342: The presentation asset owns:
343: - startup prompts and consolidated setup questions.
344: - auto fail-fast display text.
345: - dashboard and checkpoint layouts.
346: - success and failure result templates.
347: - next-step suggestions.
348: 
349: The router must not contain inline startup-question wording, dashboard templates, result templates, or next-step wording when a presentation asset exists.
350: The split is behavior-preserving: move display content, do not change routing semantics.
351: 
352: **Variants (one type, differing only by hand-off, not by required sections). Each maps to the contract's `topology` field:**
353: 
354: - Workflow-YAML-backed (`topology: mode-pair`): routes execution into `-auto.yaml` / `-confirm.yaml` workflow assets. EXECUTION TARGETS is the `| Mode | Target |` table.
355: - Direct-dispatch-script (`topology: direct-dispatch`): dispatches directly to tools or scripts, no workflow YAML. The mode table is not required.
356: - Subaction route-manifest (`topology: subaction-route-manifest`): a direct-dispatch router that resolves sub-actions through an owned `_routes.yaml` manifest.
357: - Compiled-stub: a generated stub carrying the `render-command-contract` marker whose contract is rendered at invocation. It is exempt from authored section requirements (retained variant, no command currently uses it).
358: 
359: Which family uses which topology is defined by the machine-readable command contract (`assets/command-contract.json`, validated by `assets/command-contract.schema.json`). Consult it rather than a hand-maintained family list. Use `assets/command-router-template.md` for the canonical numbered router skeleton, and `assets/command-presentation-template.md` for the full presentation asset skeleton.
360: 
361: **Template self-sufficiency.** Each router variant must be authorable from its template alone.
362: `command-router-template.md` plus the family's `command-contract.json` entry carry every section, vocabulary and asset-path shape a new router needs.
363: If a required shape is not derivable from the template and the contract, the template is incomplete.
364: Fix the template rather than copying a sibling command.
365: This keeps the contract the single source and lets `generate-command-routers.cjs --check` detect drift instead of it hiding in hand-copied prose.

## 3. BEHAVIOR-PRESERVING RULE

Moving display text into the presentation asset must not change routing semantics, required inputs, confirmation behavior, or tool permissions. ## 3. MODE ROUTING
